subsystems.name: Sorbent material
subsystems.role: captures water vapour from the air when it is cool or humid.

subsystems.name: Sorbent bed
subsystems.role: presents a large surface area to airflow for adsorption.

subsystems.name: Desorption heat source
subsystems.role: warms the sorbent to release the captured water as vapour.
parts: solar thermal collector or electric heater

subsystems.name: Condenser
subsystems.role: cools the released vapour back into liquid water.

subsystems.name: Air handling and control
subsystems.role: moves air over the sorbent and manages the adsorption–desorption cycle.

subsystems.name: Water collection and storage
subsystems.role: collects, stores and treats the product water.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the MOF
buildSteps.detail: Metal salts and organic linker molecules are mixed in solvent, heated to crystallise, then washed and dried into a fine powder.

buildSteps.title: Coat the sorbent onto a support
buildSteps.detail: The MOF is dispersed in a binder and coated onto metal fins or honeycomb to maximise surface area and air contact.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the sorbent module
buildSteps.detail: Coated fins are stacked into a cartridge that can be swapped or regenerated.

buildSteps.title: Build the enclosure and air path
buildSteps.detail: A fan, ducts and dampers direct ambient air through the sorbent bed during adsorption.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the heat source
buildSteps.detail: A solar collector or electric heater is coupled to the bed to drive off water during desorption.

buildSteps.title: Add the condenser and collection
buildSteps.detail: A cold plate or heat exchanger condenses the vapour; the liquid drains into a tank with filtration.

buildSteps.title: Install controls
buildSteps.detail: Sensors and a microcontroller automate the day–night or heat–cool cycle for maximum yield.

buildSteps.title: Field test and deploy
buildSteps.detail: Units are tested in arid conditions and connected to irrigation or drinking-water systems.

prerequisites.why: most MOFs are made in small batches; scaling up while keeping performance and cost low is still being demonstrated.
solar thermal or waste heat can drive desorption, which is essential for off-grid operation.
standard refrigeration or heat exchangers work, though condensing in hot dry air can be energy-intensive.
MOFs can degrade with repeated cycling and exposure to contaminants.
solar panels can run fans and controls, but water output per unit area is still limited.

pathway.milestone: condensation-based atmospheric water generators commercially available for humid climates (relative humidity above about 60%)
pathway.unlocks: drinking water in humid regions with limited infrastructure.

pathway.milestone: MOF-based sorption devices in pilot demonstrations for arid climates (relative humidity below about 30%)
pathway.unlocks: water production in dry regions without liquid water sources.

pathway.milestone: integration with solar power and drip irrigation for off-grid farming
large-scale, low-cost modules for community water supply
pathway.unlocks: reduced water stress in dry coastal and desert regions.
